author: /root/acceptance126
preconditions: Receive immutable committed Generator C1 and read its actual controller/stub/harness source before selecting a mutation site. C1 is not available when this plan is written.

Verify the current approved contract, API/projection and normative identities against the accepted seal; verify test bytes exactly60f679. Record C1 commit/tree, each exercised source/test/stub/schema/helper Git blob and SHA256, Python executable/version, platform and existing jsonschema package identity.

Materialize the small required committed file set from Git objects into private temporary candidate roots, without copying repository/evidence history. Case1 requires controller, sealed runner, sibling stub, verify_lib and the two runtime schemas. Account for any actual source dependency before running; do not invent a public executable-selector surface.

Each run uses the runner's fresh private state/processes/resources. A missing dependency, source absence, syntax error, startup/setup failure or unsupported action is a blocked control, never semantic red.

positive_control.cwd: Private unmodified C1 materialization with exact sealed test bytes
positive_control.required_result: Actual exit0 and PASS case1/stub. The sealed ownership test opens a real detached child, successfully sets owner-value, refuses foreign evaluate/observe, reads the unchanged value, checks role abuse and validates emitted records. Its finally cleanup runs.
positive_control.failure_disposition: Preserve exact assertion/exit/output and source identity. Diagnose setup versus an actual C1 defect before any repair; do not treat an unrelated failure as the planned mutant control.

semantic_mutant.name: foreign-owner-admission-bypass
semantic_mutant.obligation: AT4/case1 and interface.policy: foreign Generator requesters cannot execute in another owner's session, including observe.
semantic_mutant.source_change: After reading C1, identify its actual pre-dispatch foreign-owner comparison. In a separate private candidate disable only that guard for a well-shaped different Generator principal. Record exact old/new hunk and byte hashes. Preserve role, generation, lease, attempt, transport, child protocol and operation behavior; do not fake responses or modify tests. If the actual implementation cannot support this narrow single semantic change, stop and record why before proposing a different control.
semantic_mutant.assertion_location: The unchanged ownership test calls refused(..., foreign_owner) for a different Generator; Session.call asserts the actual subprocess exit before accepting a rejection record.
semantic_mutant.required_result: Actual exit1 with that exact intended assertion prefix after working open/owner mutation, because the mutant admits the foreign request. No SETUP_FAILURE or SETUP_OR_INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE may substitute for this assertion. Record the actual response/output and mutation provenance.
semantic_mutant.positive_pair: The same exact sealed command must pass on unmodified C1 before mutation. After deleting the mutant candidate, rerun that command from a fresh unmodified C1 materialization and require exit0 again, demonstrating that the single source mutation caused the behavioral failure.

cleanup: Use the sealed Session finally cleanup with independently verified private process identities. Wait for disposable candidate processes to stop before removing only their held TemporaryDirectory roots.

Preserve C1 and all historical evidence. Mutation touches only tools/runtime_session.py inside its private materialization; no shared worktree, committed test, installed payload, Generator branch or Root lifecycle field changes.

evidence.per_run: Separate stdout.txt, stderr.txt and result.json containing exact argv/cwd, actual exit, host/runtime identity, C1 identity, test/source manifest and evidence paths. Keep raw output outside JSON strings.
evidence.mutation: Record exact patch/hunk, original and mutated source hashes, preserved test hash, and the paired unmodified runs. Link immutable Git objects rather than copying nested history.
evidence.boundary: An executed narrow mutant red is sensitivity evidence against an executable C1 with positive controls. It does not establish pristine-base red, final bundle acceptance, product QA or CI conformance.
